INTERVIEW/INTERNSHIP
EXPERIENCE
Arnav Zutshi
BTech. Computer Engineering

APPLICATION
Mondelez generally comes for CE/IT branches only and during our time they only
shortlisted the CE applicants for the GD/Interview rounds. This shortlisting was based on
resume. Mondelez had come quite late for Internship.
GROUP DISCUSSION ROUND
Mondelez had shortlisted 28 students from their resume, all from CE branch. They had
come to the campus to take offline group discussions. They had divided us into 4 panels
of 7 students each for the group discussion. There was a group discussion room in the
TPO where all the GD’s were taken simultaneously. There were 2 interviewers in a GD
panel. After salutations we were briefed about the GD rules (20 minutes discussion
including the last 2 minutes to conclude). I have attached the Case Study on which the
GD was taken.
Some Tips for the GD:
●
Try and be the initiator of the discussion. You will get first some time to prepare
and jot down your points. Being the starter of the discussion has a positive impact
on the panel
●
Please put for all the points you have jot down, do not stay silent throughout the
GD
●
Also, please put all the *logical points* on the table, illogical points make a bad
impression
●
Showcase your technical knowledge using the GD
●
NEVER STAY SILENT!
●
If someone has put a point, do not repeat that, but you can go ahead and extend
that point to put your thoughts in it
●
Do not raise your voice to be heard, but also at the same time be pushy to put
your point (not aggressive), people there will not give you a chance to speak
●
Keep track of time, once the panel says that last 2 minutes, do not put any more
points, just conclude the discussion, putting points in the concluding time portrays
as bad impression
1

INTERVIEW
After the GD round, 4 students were selected from each panel (a total of 16 students) for
the interview round. The interviews were taken by a different set of people (not the one’s
in your GD). This was the only interview. I was first asked to introduce myself. I was then
asked about my resume, told to explain my projects and any additional stack/functionality
I would like to add to my project. They specifically took interest in one of my blockchain
projects on which the discussion went for long. Then the HR also asked about the
learnings other then technology from these projects. HR also asked the most stressfull
period in college life. Moving on the tech interviewer asked me about my family
background, my education background and then gave some cases of what technology I
would use for each situations that he had given me. I was then asked if inhouse technical
team is better or out-sourcing the development is better. I was asked about the
committees I had joined and the work I did there (My learnings). There was some more
chit-chat and the interview was over.
RESULT
A total of 7 students were selected after the interview round for the internship. They had
an induction program too where they gave a basket full of their products which I
obviously loved!
To all aspiring, ALL THE BEST!!
3

INTERNSHIP
Giving a broad overviewof my experience, it was fantastic! I was allotted work under Digital
Workplace tower and was given 2 projects, one was a managerial project (I worked as a project
manager) the other project was of web-development and office-365 development (dealing with
Azure, Exchange, SharePoint). The work environment is very chill, there is work from home option
(though they say it is compulsory to come for 3 days in a week but you can go ahead and stay at
home, they have no problem). Everyone at work is really friendly and always ready to help. Since
it is an MNC, dealing with people internationally was a very great experience. They have flexible
working hours (usually I would enter office at 10.30 and leave around 3). Most of the work is done
on the laptops (MS Teams meetings) so there is no compulsion to come to the office. Some of my
other peers were working on data analytics, AR/VR, Blockchain, NLP and Kubernetes(Cloud). My
advise would be to stick to your project and do not grieve if you think you got a very easy or
non-impactfull project because in the end the project was assigned by your manager and he/she
knows how to evaluate you based on the same. The plus point on going to the office was the free
oreos you could eat all day. My manager was from UK and we only had communication via teams.
The project allotted to me was still a little left but there was a smooth handover to my team,
although some of the portals were developed by me. Majorly the technologies i worked on
included (TypeScript, SPFx Framework, SharePoint, Exchange, Azure, Office 365).
4
